reviews.text:
I had been hand washing dishes for five years, and was getting so sick of it, I felt like I was going nuts and that it was the only thing I was ever doing! I vowed to never move again to a place with no dishwasher but alas this apartment was so nice except for that fact (and also met my other criteria: a thermostat I could control for the first time in five years), so I went for it. Once moved in, hand washing dishes was even tougher than usual because the sink was only one basin, not two like most kitchen sinks! I had noticed that before moving in, but I didn't think about what an annoyance that would be. So, I jokingly asked for a dishwasher for my birthday, took measurements, figured out which one to ask for, and amazingly, Mom actually got it for me! Thank you, Mommy!

So I have had this thing for five months now; I think that qualifies me to speak about it. I LOVE it. I am so ecstatic to not have to hand wash dishes anymore, sometimes I just look at it in amazement.

Although my place is nice, it is an efficiency, so my kitchen, living room, and bedroom are all in one big room. Despite this, the dishwasher noise is hardly obtrusive even while sleeping. I mean, sometimes I notice the noise and maybe have to turn the TV up a couple notches, but it is a no-brainer trade-off compared to hand-washing all the time! The unit does beep eight times upon completion but even that becomes unobtrusive once you get used to it.

Depending on how many dishes/pots/pans build-up or how many I use to make a meal, I sometimes can't fit everything in, but I would not call this factor an issue at all.

The only suggestions I have are, 1) read the owner's manual front-to-back to familiarize yourself with everything; 2) as the owner's manual suggests, every couple weeks or so (depending on how messy your stuff is when you put it in), take the drawer out, and then take the two pieces out of the \\"floor\\" of the washer (the white plastic cylindricalthing and the metal mesh square thing), and rinse them off thoroughly (I also use the kitchen sink hose to rinse out the inside of the until when I do this and let it drain into the hole). If you don't do this, you will start to notice lots of bits left on your dishes; but MOST importantly, 3) If anything such as a large utensil, leaning dinner plates, a pot, etc. is leaning into the indented area on the front of the drawer by the utensil holder and soap holder (when door is closed), it will block the soap door from opening all the way at the time of release, and when your load finishes, you will see some soap still in the soap thing. This area must be kept pretty clear so the little soap door has room to open all the way. Another relatively minor issue is that, at least in my case, the low drying agent indicator light doesn't always come on when the drying agent is low or empty, so you just have to keep your eye on that little port every so often (there is something about that in the manual).

To me, these problems are practically non-issues and I think this is a fabulous dishwasher! I will write again if any other issues ever arise.

My wife and I live in an apartment with a weirdly shaped kitchen. The kitchen also has no counter space other than right next to the kitchen sink. Between the kitchen table, buffet, china hutch, bookcase and two rolling carts all of our floor space was taking up, so we didn't have room for a bigger dishwasher. We also really enjoy hosting, we've had as many as 12 over for dinner parties, and 12 guests make for a lot of dishes. We found that the small footprint of this dishwasher fits perfectly next to our kitchen sink, and since it can do up to 6 place settings at a time it handles everything in just two passes. Not bad for a small unit. As a bonus for us because of it's small size, we can use it for all of our daily dishes without anything having to sit for too long because it wasn't full enough to make it worthwhile to run. We usually run it about twice a week.

Set up is a breeze on the unit as well. I was able to get it out of the box and running in less than an hour, taking my time to make sure all of the connections were secure. The unit is not that loud either, which is nice. You know it's running, but's it's not distracting. We had it running, but were still able to have a lovely conversation over desserts with the unit less than 10 feet away.

The only thing that keeps this from being a 5 star rating is that I wish the inside was a 1\\" taller. We have some plates that are slightly bigger than standard, they fit but they make it hard to put anything else in. All in all this is a great unit at an outstanding price. We've had it for over two months using it regularly and it works as advertised. Can't really ask for much more than that.

reviews.text:
Update Oct 2014 - I've had this for almost three years now and it still works great. I just bought this cart to sit it on which is a VAST and sturdy improvement over what I had been using, I would highly recommend it. Each shelf holds 266 pounds. [[ASIN:B008ALBHWQ TRINITY EcoStorage 3-Tier NSF Chrome Cart]].

Update - April 2012 and it still is working great. Once you figure out how to load it and what works it becomes really easy, I wouldn't trade it !

I think if you have had a problem with the dishes getting clean you first want to check your water hardness and rinse agent. Also you need to make sure you run your water and it is HOT before you attach the hoses to start the dishes. If you don't have the hoses attached tight enough or properly, it's going to leak. Every time I plug it in, I always give the hoses a glance just in case, since I am moving it back and forth. Also I have to drain the hoses into a bowl after each wash. I lift the hose high in the air and even more water flows into the bowl I use for that purpose.
-----
Quick facts -

- It's packed really well, it will take you more than a few minutes to get it out of all the packing.

-I have this on a cart that is 19x27.5 . It fits great with about 5 inches left on the end, and an inch in the front. Make sure it is a sturdy kitchen cart I would recommend. It would not fit under my cabinets, I needed one more inch.

-When you first get it out of the box and before you start doing the dishes on a regular basis the drain hoses will be less pliable, just make sure that the connections on the back are tight before you turn the water on and you will be good to go. The second time I used it some water sprayed out because we had been moving the hoses to drain the extra water.

-You do have to change your faucet head. (!!!!!!) ( They supply the one you need ! ) If you've already had a portable dishwasher you already know this. Acheapy faucet in general is probably the only way you will be making the new connection fit easily. It just screws on to your faucet head fairly easily if you have a regular plain old faucet. We actually had to take out the faucet we had before for a cheaper version, but that was worth it not to do dishes by hand and being that we didn't want to tear out cabinets and pay someone to install a built in.

- Read the placement chart for the dishes. Big plates go up front and they should fit fine. I do cups on the side, bowls along the back along with small plates where I can fit them.

- The water usage is listed as liters on the cycle chart in the manual, not gallons. A normal wash will use about 3.5 gallons of water, or 13.6 liters.

-------------------------
When we first got it and my husband looked inside he asked \\"do you like this ?\\" with a note of pessimism. And I was unsure at first because it was smaller.

I've gone from a full size portable to this size after the first one broke fairly quickly.

This size works well for a family of 4. Sometimes I do 2-3 loads a day. It depends of what I've cooked. Usually it's 1-2.

It might be small, but it cleans the dishes well.

Cycle info -

You can do a regular load of lightly soiled dishes with milk and juice residue, crumbs and ketchup, in 50 minutes on the light cycle that doesn't have a dry time. It's called speed and it is 30 minutes less than light, it just doesn't take 30 minutes to dry the dishes. So a lot of times, that will work for me. When you open the the door a lot of steam escapes and they get dry quickly enough on their own. The normal cycle has 3 pre rinses, and 1 wash cycle, and 2 rinses. The speed cycle has 2 pre-rinses and 1 wash cycle and 1 rinse.

I've used all kinds of detergent and they all work well. I am using a powder at the moment.

And also, I think it is common sense that you have to be careful that the spatula or other objects don't obstruct the spinning arm below the basket. It could maybe use a few more well placed built in metal tines if I could think of any improvements.

I bought a square trade warranty after my last issue with a portable, not sure that I will need it, but you can search for the appliance one for the 250-300 dollar coverage.

Despite following instructions pertaining to putting in \\"one more item\\" mid-cycle, 50% of the time, closing door, machine starts without notice and drains half of its water, then proceeds with the rest of the cycle without enough water to complete it (it just sits there grinding its motor).

Problem not specific to a unit as I tried two units (the first arrived with a broken spray arm). It's sad because the unit is otherwise well built.

Machine limited to plates 9\\" diameter and smaller.

Do Not Buy the SD-2201. If SPT can fix the rack design and the oddly-behaving controls, I'd buy another of their products, but they really have to fix that dish rack/spray arm design and the bizarre-behaving controls.

Hooking it up was a breeze! Very very simple.

reviews.text:
This dishwasher is absolutely wonderful. Was easy to set up (except be sure to push the washer arm down into place - mine had come out in shipping despite being very well packaged, no biggie). I can't believe how many dishes fit and get washed so thoroughly in this little thing! It does a perfect job of washing dishes. The hose goes on & off the faucet with ease in 2 seconds using their supplied adaptor. Seems very sturdy and well made. My only complaint was that the instructions tell you to be sure to use dishwasher detergent \\"with chemicals\\". This is ridiculous - you can now purchase natural dishwasher detergent at most health food stores, and the one I am using works like a charm (Seventh Generation Automatic Dishwashing Detergent). My kitchen is tiny but this guy fits perfectly between counter and cupboard. I can't believe I waited so long to get a dishwasher, what a time saver!!!

Update after using it daily for over 3 years: Love it even more!!! I have never had a single problem with it. Completely dependable and does a great job cleaning my dishes. Still using the natural dishwasher detergent with excellent results.
reviews.title: LOVE IT!!!

reviews.text:
I love my new countertop dishwasher. I've been using it for more than a week. No more dirty dishes on the counter waiting to be washed in addition to no more dish washing!
Here are some things to know:
1. It's heavy and comes in a big box. You may need someone to help you with it.
2. Run the water until it gets hot before attaching the dishwasher hose.
3. Follow the diagrams for loading the basket. If your dishes don't face toward the center of the dishwasher, they won't get cleaned.
4. There's absolutely no information about the manufacturer in the manual. There's no way to contact them.
5. There's absolutely no information about ordering parts in the manual. Guess you're out of luck if you need a replacement part.
Comment 4 and 5 resulted in a four-star review.

This dishwasher appears to be very well made but, as I said I have only had it a week and time will tell how durable it really is.    As for cleaning a large load of dishes this dishwasher does an outstanding job! Does it hold up to six place settings? Everybody's dishes are different and it holds about four and then some for me. For those of you who are wondering if this washer drains the water by gravity or it is pumped out I believe it is pumped out but, I could not find any documentation on this. Very easy to hookup to you kitchen faucet. Does a great job drying the dishes.    Update 10/26/2011: Dishwasher performs perfectly! Here are some additional thoughts - It says it in the directions that come with the dishwasher but make sure you add your dishwasher powder just before you start the wash not 2 hours earlier or it will harden. reviews.title: SPT Countertop Dishwasher  Model: SD-2201W

reviews.text:
After receiving this in a huge package today, I opened it up to quickly find that it had a good sized ding on the right of the outer shell. After inspecting it inside, it didn't look like anything had been damaged beyond cosmetic so I didn't think it would be worth paying $80 shipping to send it back and get it replaced for something irrelevant. At the worst I thought some insulation would of been compressed in the particular area. I also have no idea how it got damaged as it was put in two layers of some serious packaging.

I hooked everything up after setting it on the counter and loaded it with dishes. Hit the power button, set it to heavy load, and pressed start. I heard a humming noise as it started to fill with water. This continued for about a minute until I suddenly heard a CLICK! Followed by the sound of water pouring. At first I thought it was internal, until I saw a waterfall coming down off of my counter and onto the floor. I quickly unplugged it, turned the water off, and grabbed a towel. I thought that maybe a washer around the seal wasn't properly seated or something, but upon lifting the unit up to gaze under it, there were two holes in the bottom right next to each other with water gushing out of them.

I'm going to call the company tomorrow morning to see if this is a known issue and is something I can fix myself. I really don't want to spend $80 to ship it and get it serviced.

reviews.text: Wasn't quite sure what to expect with this dishwasher.  For all intents and purposed couldn't ask for anything better.  Arrived well packaged, very easy setup.  Did so after dinner, had kids put dishes aside while I cleaned the counter space and hooked it all up and had to buy the rinse and detergent aid.  By the time I had it ready, the left over remants of cheesy mashed potatoes were well dried on the kids plates.  Completely clean and sparkly after the cycle was complete. Works very well on counter top, quick release to the water tap is a snap.  LOve it.. Will update if any problems arise...so far no leaks for the get go..
reviews.title: Impressed! Very Awesome

reviews.text:
I just bought this dishwasher and was thrilled at how quickly it arrived. I purchased it on Wednesday and it arrived on Thursday! Tracking was a breeze. Once I unpacked the unit, I was surprised at how light it was.

It came with all the parts to install it to my sink's faucet, though it did take me a few minutes to discover the plastic hookup actually had the faucet adaptor inside it. Once I pulled the metal faucet adapter out and screwed it onto my sink's faucet - I was ready to go. I hooked up all the tubes - be careful not to over tighten them, but get them tight! I plugged the unit in and turned on the water. No leaks so I put a few dishes in and started the washer last night.

The unit is surprisingly quiet (for a dishwasher) and it takes awhile for the load to run. Once the load was finished I just open the door to let everything dry out. Tonight will be my second try with the dishwasher. So far everything is good, no leaks. I set the unit up on a kitchen cart with wheels so I can just move it to the sink when I'm ready to use it.
The silver color is nice and the door design is very simple. No buttons to press before you can open the door or close it. Just a simple pull or push to shut it. When the unit is powered, opening or closing the door results in a beep.

This is an energy star efficient washer, so I'm hoping it saves me on time and water (hand washing dishes tends to take me more water than this unit uses).

I will try and edit or add another review once I've had the unit a little longer.

categories.name: Leaks & water containment
categories.description: Water escaping from the base, hoses, or fittings onto counters and floors.

categories.name: Wash & dry performance
categories.description: Dishes not getting clean, dried, or rinsed properly during cycles.

categories.name: Capacity & counter fit
categories.description: Interior space, plate fit, and how much room the unit takes in the kitchen.

categories.name: Setup, hookup & instructions
categories.description: Faucet adapters, hoses, and documentation needed to install and operate the unit.

categories.name: Reliability & durability
categories.description: Component failures and breakdowns after weeks to a couple of years of use.

categories.name: Shipping, support & returns
categories.description: Condition on arrival, manufacturer responsiveness, and the cost of sending a heavy unit back.

painPoints.name: Standard dinner plates don't fit the rack
painPoints.description: Customers find that standard 10-11 inch dinner plates won't stand upright in the rack, so they can only load a place setting or two, switch to smaller plates, or hand-wash their larger dishware. Because interior dimensions aren't published, buyers only discover the limit after the unit arrives.
painPoints.proposedResponse: Publish interior rack dimensions and a maximum plate diameter in the product description and manual, with a photo of a loaded rack holding standard plates, and redesign the rack tine spacing/angle so 11 inch plates seat upright.

painPoints.name: Rear inlet and drain hose fittings leak
painPoints.description: Supply and drain connectors at the rear leak on first use or after months of use, and plastic nuts arrive cracked or split during hook-up and back off once the line pressurises. Customers re-tighten with pliers or add teflon tape, washers or o-rings, and some have had water puddle on and warp their counters.
painPoints.proposedResponse: Replace the plastic inlet/drain nuts with metal or reinforced fittings, ship pre-installed washers or o-rings, and add a torque warning plus a leak-check step to the setup instructions.

painPoints.name: Unit takes more counter space than expected
painPoints.description: The unit is taller and bulkier than product photos suggest, swallowing much of a small kitchen counter and frequently not clearing overhanging upper cabinets. Buyers end up putting it on a rolling rack, doing carpentry, or moving it out of the kitchen entirely.
painPoints.proposedResponse: Add exact external height, width and depth plus a required clearance figure to the top of the listing, along with a printable measuring guide and a scale photo of the unit under standard cabinets.

painPoints.name: Dishes come out dirty unless pre-washed by hand
painPoints.description: Food residue, dried-on chunks and film survive the cycle, so customers pre-rinse or scrub before loading and re-wash afterwards. Several report that only the heavier pots-and-pans setting cleans properly, and that tall glasses don't get clean inside on light or regular cycles.
painPoints.proposedResponse: Test spray coverage and water temperature on the light and regular cycles against tall glassware and dried-on soil, and adjust cycle time, spray pattern and heating so a normal cycle cleans without pre-washing; until then, state the pre-scrape and loading requirements explicitly in the manual and listing.

painPoints.name: Faucet adapter won't fit common faucets
painPoints.description: The quick-connect adapter doesn't mate with pull-down, Moen, Delta, filtered and older non-standard faucets, so customers stack hardware-store reducers, hire a plumber, plumb a separate line, or return the unit. The manufacturer reportedly does not supply alternative adapters.
painPoints.proposedResponse: Ship an adapter kit covering the common faucet thread sizes, publish a compatibility list with the specific faucet types that do not work, and make individual adapters orderable directly from support.

painPoints.name: Dishes stay wet; no effective drying
painPoints.description: There is no effective drying, so dishes, plastics and the tub are still wet when the cycle ends and customers towel-dry or leave the door ajar for hours. Concave items such as goblet feet and bowls hold water and detergent residue.
painPoints.proposedResponse: Add a heated or fan-assisted dry phase, or if that isn't feasible on this platform, state plainly in the listing and manual that no dry cycle is included and that a rinse aid is required, and revise rack geometry so bowls and goblet feet drain.

painPoints.name: Manual is vague, poorly translated and incomplete
painPoints.description: The manual doesn't clearly explain hose hook-up and tightening, the buttons, water-hardness salt, or how to tell a cycle has finished, and installation steps sit at the back. Customers can't interpret the beeps and flashing lights and fall back on trial and error; some units arrive with no manual at all.
painPoints.proposedResponse: Rewrite the manual with a native-English technical writer: step-by-step illustrated installation at the front, a beep/light code table, a salt and detergent section, and a parts-ordering page, plus a downloadable PDF and short setup video linked from the listing.

painPoints.name: Unit arrives dented, cracked or with broken parts
painPoints.description: Units arrive with dented panels, cracked doors or cases, and broken spray arms, wheels, tablet baskets or faucet adapters, sometimes inside an undamaged outer box. Replacement units have arrived damaged too, so the problem repeats.
painPoints.proposedResponse: Redesign inner packaging to brace the door, spray arm and base, drop-test the new pack, and stock the small breakables (tablet basket, spray arm, wheels, adapter) as free spare parts shipped on request instead of requiring a whole-unit return.

painPoints.name: Water pours from the base and floods the floor
painPoints.description: Water escapes from underneath the machine around the pump/motor area or through holes in the plastic base rather than from the hose connections, flooding counters and floors. It hits some owners on the first run and others after weeks or months, and reviewers report receiving replacement units that leaked as well.
painPoints.proposedResponse: Run a teardown and pressure/leak test on returned units to identify the failing seal or base joint, then correct the assembly and add an end-of-line water test before shipping; in parallel, offer immediate replacement or refund without requiring the customer to ship the unit back.

painPoints.name: Spray arm hits the rack and won't rotate
painPoints.description: The wash arm catches on the dish rack even with the machine empty, sometimes because the metal floor isn't seated on arrival and sometimes because the rack sits too low. The cycle stalls or the load comes out unwashed until the owner bends the rack wheel holders or forces the floor down.
painPoints.proposedResponse: Add an assembly check that the tub floor is fully seated before packing, increase clearance between spray arm and rack, and include a first-run instruction to spin the arm by hand with a picture of correct rack height.

painPoints.name: Control buttons and power stop responding
painPoints.description: After a few weeks to about a year the power switch or control panel stops accepting input, the unit freezes with lights on, or it switches itself on and off at random. Power cycling doesn't recover it and the machine becomes unusable, with at least one owner finding factory service didn't fix it.
painPoints.proposedResponse: Collect and bench-test failed control panels and power switches to determine whether the fault is the membrane switch, the board or moisture ingress, then correct the part and stock control panels as a field-replaceable spare.

painPoints.name: Manufacturer support and warranty go unanswered
painPoints.description: Owners reporting leaks and failures get no reply from manufacturer email or phone, cannot obtain parts, and get no warranty service. Some are told to buy a new machine rather than repair, or are simply pointed at a hardware store.
painPoints.proposedResponse: Staff a support queue with a published response-time commitment and case tracking, create a parts catalogue with ordering, and define a warranty decision path so agents can authorise replacement or refund without sending customers away.

painPoints.name: Cycles run long and tie up the sink
painPoints.description: Wash cycles run from around 45 minutes to two hours, longer than the manual indicates, and the shorter cycles don't clean well enough to be a real alternative. Since the adapter occupies the faucet, the kitchen sink is unusable for the whole run.
painPoints.proposedResponse: Correct the stated cycle times in the manual and listing, and add a faucet adapter with a diverter or bypass tap so the sink stays usable while the machine runs.

painPoints.name: Detergent dispenser fails to release soap
painPoints.description: The detergent cup stays shut or is still full of undissolved detergent and sludge after a cycle, leaving the load merely rinsed. Owners trace it to a loaded plate blocking the door, a broken plastic latch, pods put in the dispenser rather than the basket, or a dispenser that wasn't dry when filled.
painPoints.proposedResponse: Strengthen the dispenser latch, relocate or shield the door so loaded dishes can't block it, and add clear labelling plus manual instructions on where pods versus powder go and on drying the cup before filling.

painPoints.name: Unit clogs, won't drain, and errors mid-cycle
painPoints.description: Machines stop shortly after starting with prolonged beeping, flashing lights or a false overflow or low-pressure error, or run the drain pump without washing. Others stop draining after months, leaving dirty soapy water in the tub and residue on dishes, and the drain button sometimes does nothing so owners drain by hand with the hoses.
painPoints.proposedResponse: Diagnose the overflow/low-pressure sensor and drain pump on returned units to separate false-trip sensing from genuine clogs, then fix the trigger logic and add a user-serviceable filter with a documented clearing procedure and error-code table.

painPoints.name: Motor grows loud; drain phase especially noisy
painPoints.description: Units that were quiet when new develop loud buzzing, whining or grinding within weeks to months, including on replacement units. Even healthy machines are loud during the drain phase, loud enough that owners pause the TV in the next room.
painPoints.proposedResponse: Measure noise on new and field-returned units through the drain phase to identify whether the pump runs dry or cavitates, then revise the pump mount or drain sequence and note expected drain-phase noise in the manual.

painPoints.name: Customer pays $50-$100 freight to return heavy unit
painPoints.description: Returning or getting warranty repair on the unit means repacking a heavy appliance and paying freight to California, which some customers physically can't do or can't pack because they no longer have the box. Refund requests also go unanswered or are slow, and at least one customer was billed twice after a return went missing.
painPoints.proposedResponse: Introduce prepaid freight labels and, where the fault is clear, replacement without return, plus tracked return receipts so refunds trigger automatically rather than waiting on warehouse reconciliation.

painPoints.name: Short, stiff hoses restrict placement and won't drain
painPoints.description: The supply and drain hoses are short, stiff and metric-sized with no extension available, which limits where the unit can go and makes routing awkward. There is nowhere to hang the drain line, and because the hoses can't be drained, leftover water spills on the counter or floor when the unit is moved.
painPoints.proposedResponse: Offer a longer flexible hose set and a metric-to-standard extension as accessories, add hose and cord clips or a hanger to the rear of the cabinet, and provide a drain step in the manual for emptying residual water before moving.

recommendations.title: Root-cause and stop base leaks with an end-of-line water test
recommendations.summary: Teardown and pressure-test returned units leaking from the base, fix the failing seal or base joint, and add a water test before every unit ships.
recommendations.reasoning: Base leaks are the most damaging failure in the dataset: critical severity (3.8 mean) with an average rating of 1.6 across all analysed reviews, and customers describe counters and floors "absolutely flooded". Although it sits in watch-closely at 2.9% of all analysed reviews, the property damage and reports of replacements leaking too justify a now horizon. Rear fitting leaks share the same water-containment test, so fixing both under one leak-test gate is efficient.

recommendations.title: Replace plastic hose nuts with metal fittings and pre-fitted seals
recommendations.summary: Swap the cracking plastic inlet and drain nuts for metal or reinforced fittings with pre-installed washers, and add a torque warning and leak check to setup.
recommendations.reasoning: Rear fitting leaks appear in 5.3% of all analysed reviews at moderate severity (2.2) in the improve-at-scale quadrant, and customers report "the nuts are plastic, I accidentally over tightened the nut on the outlet hose and ended up cracking it". The fix is a component substitution with a clear failure mode, and because it causes water on counters it belongs alongside the leak work now.

recommendations.title: Make the normal wash cycle clean without hand pre-washing
recommendations.summary: Retune spray coverage, temperature and duration on light and regular cycles so dried-on soil and tall glasses come clean without pre-scrubbing.
recommendations.reasoning: Poor cleaning is in the fix-first quadrant at 7.6% of all analysed reviews with 2.4 mean severity and a 3.0 average rating, the lowest-rated of the high-frequency issues. Customers say "I always have gunk and residue leftover whenever I attempt to use them" and that only pots-and-pans works. Spray arm fouling on the rack is a mechanical contributor to unwashed loads, so it is investigated in the same workstream.

recommendations.title: Ship a multi-faucet adapter kit and publish a compatibility list
recommendations.summary: Include adapters for the common faucet thread sizes, list the faucet types that will not connect, and let customers order adapters from support.
recommendations.reasoning: Adapter incompatibility is fix-first at 3.2% of all analysed reviews with 2.3 mean severity, and it blocks first use entirely: customers call plumbers, buy hardware-store reducers, or return the unit. Because the manufacturer reportedly supplies no alternative adapters, a kit plus a published compatibility list removes the failure and the return.

recommendations.title: Publish exact dimensions, cabinet clearance and max plate size
recommendations.summary: Put external dimensions, required cabinet clearance and interior rack capacity with a maximum plate diameter at the top of the listing and in the manual.
recommendations.reasoning: Together these are the two most frequent issues in the dataset, at 9.9% and 8.4% of all analysed reviews, and both are expectation failures discovered after delivery: "This dishwasher does take up our entire right side counter- so it is rather big- bigger than I had expected" and plates that "do not fit". Both sit in improve-at-scale with moderate severity, but disclosure is a listing change that prevents the surprise immediately, so it goes now.

recommendations.title: Redesign the rack so standard 11-inch plates seat upright
recommendations.summary: Change tine spacing and angle in the dish rack so full-size dinner plates load upright without wedging, and raise clearance over the spray arm.
recommendations.reasoning: Plate fit is the highest-priority pain point at 9.9% of all analysed reviews, but at 2.0 mean severity in improve-at-scale it is a satisfaction ceiling rather than a failure, so hardware redesign follows the disclosure fix. Rack geometry also drives the spray arm catching on the rack, where customers had to "bend the racks wheel holders down a bit to raise the dish rack", making one rack revision address both.

recommendations.title: Rewrite the manual with illustrated setup and an error-code table
recommendations.summary: Produce a native-English manual with step-by-step installation at the front, a beep and flashing-light code table, salt and detergent sections, and a parts page, plus a PDF and setup video.
recommendations.reasoning: Manual quality shows up in 3.9% of all analysed reviews in improve-at-scale, and customers report it is "full of engrish and typos, and was extremely unhelpful" and that they cannot tell what the beeps mean. The same document is where corrected cycle times, the no-dry-cycle and rinse-aid requirement, error codes, detergent placement and hose draining need to be stated, so one rewrite closes several gaps at once.

recommendations.title: Add a faucet diverter so the sink stays usable during a cycle
recommendations.summary: Supply an adapter with a bypass tap and correct the published cycle times so owners are not cut off from the kitchen sink for hours.
recommendations.reasoning: Long cycles blocking the sink appear in 5.3% of all analysed reviews in improve-at-scale, with low severity (1.5) but a concrete complaint: "You CANNOT use your sink for the couple hours it takes the dishwasher (on heavy cycle) to run". A diverter is a small accessory change that pairs naturally with the adapter kit work already planned.

recommendations.title: Repack for shipping and ship small spare parts on request
recommendations.summary: Brace the door, spray arm and base in new inner packaging, drop-test it, and stock tablet baskets, spray arms, wheels and adapters as free spares instead of full returns.
recommendations.reasoning: Arrival damage is fix-first at 3.2% of all analysed reviews with 2.3 mean severity, and it occurs inside undamaged outer boxes, pointing at inner packaging rather than carriers. It also feeds the return burden, where customers face freight on a heavy unit and say "I want to return it but do not have a box large enough to return it", so spares dispatch resolves many cases without a return.

recommendations.title: Staff manufacturer support with case tracking and prepaid returns
recommendations.summary: Create a tracked support queue with a published response commitment, a parts catalogue, warranty authority for agents, and prepaid freight or replacement-without-return for clear faults.
recommendations.reasoning: Unanswered support and costly returns both average 1.6 and 1.4 star ratings across all analysed reviews at major severity, with customers reporting "I reached out to the manufacter by suggested email, but received no response" and being told to buy a new machine. These are the destination for critical reliability failures such as dead control panels and mid-cycle drain errors, so support capability must land before those hardware fixes reach the field.

recommendations.title: Bench-test failed control panels and stock them as spares
recommendations.summary: Analyse returned units whose power switch or panel stops responding to isolate the failing component, correct it, and make the panel a field-replaceable part.
recommendations.reasoning: Control and power failures are critical severity (3.7) with a 2.0 average rating across all analysed reviews, and the machine becomes unusable: "After three of years the buttons stopped working making inoperable." At 1.6% of all analysed reviews it sits in watch-closely, so it follows the leak and wash work, but the diagnosis overlaps with the false overflow and drain errors and should run together.

method.discoverySamplingRule: A rating column was mapped (scale 1–5), so discovery favoured critical reviews: all 162 reviews rated ≤ 3 (60% of the scale maximum) were included, and the remaining 438 of the 600 sample places were filled with the other reviews ranked by their score on the built-in complaint-word lexicon (ties broken by a seeded shuffle, seed 42).

warnings: 55 reviews exceed 2,000 characters; only the first 2,000 characters were classified.
1 quoted phrase in the model-written descriptions or roadmap reasoning could not be verified against the reviews and is shown without quotation marks.
